description: The certified lockstep set: these tool versions were verified TOGETHER. Re-certified 2026-08-14, on the art layer. What was run: the mission re-ran end to end and graded its three candidates 40 / 55 / 60, selecting lot_demo_001.candidate.seed_5219; check_all reports gdscript, stairs and steps clean; the portable package opened in a clean Godot project with zero plugins, zero autoloads and zero external references, 18.6 MB across 212 entries; four deli_counter shell fixes were engine-confirmed, taking nav_gate from 7 of 135 shells failing to 3. What was NOT run and is therefore not covered by this set: the walk sweep (library_walk, needs Godot, about an hour for 20 sites), the pack load check, and the lot and deli_counter unit suites. What is known failing: check_all freshness reports 57 buildings whose geometry no longer matches the spec or builder that made them, and three demo shells -- cbp, night_pawn and primos_pizza -- still fail nav_gate; none of the three is in the lot_demo_001 draw, and cbp fails on a first floor fragmented across 63 islands rather than on the stair geometry the other fixes addressed. PRIOR CERTIFICATION, 2026-07-28: All five category5_baie_dore_001 candidates now prove the mission spine: 0 of 31 legs failing on every one, 0 stranded anchors, 0 anchors without standing room, against a baseline that morning of four of four failing with nine legs each -- and seed 5421 had never been walktested at all. Four of the five come back ok=true. Seed 5017 does not, and the reason is the walktest working: its path proofs all pass and all four simulated walkers then stop at the same point, (20.5, 0.9, -2.7), on the same leg, having reached 8 of 16 targets. A route the polygon graph says exists that a physical capsule cannot walk is the collision-trap class PASS 2 was built for, and no path query can see it. Two defects, in series. A marker is where a thing IS; an anchor is where a body has to stand to use it, and the pipeline had never distinguished them, so sixteen of twenty-one anchors were demanding walkable routes onto cashier counters and into vault blocks (Lot 0.29.0). And LT_ROUTE_NEVER_COMPLETED -- Laser Tag reporting a navigability fact from a firefight -- blocked one candidate, which under fail-fast meant that candidate's walktest never dispatched at all while its stable out/ kept a seven-hour-old report that read as a current answer (Level Factory 0.20.0). NOT covered by this set: WALKTEST_ENFORCED is still False, so the walktest WARNS rather than blocks -- navigability is currently ungated, because the Laser Tag route gate was removed before its replacement was switched on. Flipping it is the next decision and every candidate has now been measured by it. The existing Phase 4 library has still never been walktested, and portfolio approval still awaits the visual-score art leg. Level Factory 0.22.0 removes the reason WALKTEST_ENFORCED could not be flipped: a candidate-scoped failure no longer halts the run. The flip is now a decision rather than a blocked one, waiting only on seed 5017's stuck walker being classified as a level defect or a walker-steering one -- Lot 0.30.0 makes the next run say which. The twenty registered mission sites were re-walked on 2026-07-28 with the fixed Lot, bypassing Level Factory entirely. SEVENTEEN of twenty come back clean, with zero stranded anchors, zero rooms that failed to bake and every mission spine walkable across twenty different site geometries -- so the anchor work generalises rather than fitting the one casino it was found on. The three that fail do so identically: every path proof passing and all four walkers pressed against a stair ramp with a HORIZONTAL contact normal, on a route the navmesh produced. That is roadmap item 16 and it is the largest thing still open: the bake and the colliders disagree about the same staircase, and the twenty `runtime_walktest: pass` stamps in the mission registry predate every fix in this set and should not be trusted until they are re-earned.

deli_counter.note: owns the collision contract; agent_contract.json is the source the Lot clearance math derives from

laser_tag.note: pinned from 0.8.0 onward. It reported UNKNOWN until then not because the addon had no version -- plugin.cfg always declared one -- but because the repo had no root VERSION file, which is the only place verify-manifest looks. The two are mirrors and the lasertag lint job fails if they disagree. Cache invalidation still rests on content, not on this line: the Level Factory adapter hashes addons/laser_tag_tool into fingerprint_inputs, so an addon edited without a bump still invalidates.

level_factory.note: 0.14.0 removed the scheduler's resume pre-skip. 0.15.0 added the walktest_navqa stage. 0.18.0 splits one anchor code into four, because a room that did not bake, an anchor that connects to nothing, a marker inside the furniture and a marker sealed behind a breach panel send a reader to four different places. 0.18.1 makes _finding coerce `location`. 0.19.0 adds WALKTEST_ANCHOR_BEHIND_BARRIER. 0.20.0 stops LT_ROUTE_NEVER_COMPLETED blocking -- the walktest measures that claim directly and Laser Tag's number is confounded by stuck bots, team wipes and a 180 s clock -- and adds RunSummary.never_dispatched, printed by cmd_run, because fail-fast leaves jobs unrun whose out/ still holds the previous run's artifacts and nothing distinguished that from success. 0.21.0 carries the walker's contact into WALKTEST_WALKER_STUCK. 0.22.0 scopes failure: a candidate-scoped job that fails eliminates that CANDIDATE and the run continues. Five candidates are generated so the weak ones can be dropped, and mission-wide fail-fast meant one bad candidate took the other four down with it -- which is why the walktest could not be enforced.

lot.note: cover clearance and lane pinch are derived from the Deli Counter agent contract, not hardcoded. 0.28.0 emits nav-QA anchors on their room's FLOOR (read from the room record, not derived from story x 4) and merges markers that coincide once dropped; the director searches the anchor's own storey plane for standing room, with a band that is asymmetric on purpose -- a body height down, one max_climb plus a voxel up. 0.29.0 resolves an anchor whose nearest standing room is on a component nothing reaches to the nearest CONNECTED one, bounded by the same 6 m, and reports both distances; it also unions clusters on MUTUAL reachability, because arrival is judged within SNAP_MAX of the destination and one directed edge had been enough. 0.30.0 makes a stuck walker record WHAT it is stuck against -- every slide collision with collider name and contact normal, plus the waypoint it was steering to. An empty contact list is the answer that matters: a capsule stopped in open space touching nothing is this tool's steering giving up rather than a level defect, and the two were indistinguishable. 0.31.0 stops _conclude's fixed key list eating the walker diagnostics it had just recorded. 0.32.0 applies gravity only while airborne and probes three step heights instead of one, and says WHICH probe failed -- no headroom to lift is a finding about the stairwell, no room ahead is a finding about the obstacle.

pipeline.note: Phase 4 complete: 100 configs / 36 families / 20 missions / 8 heroes registered, engine-gated; approval awaits visual scores
